comment: tactical-diplomat bot band for --sim 5000 --policy tactical-pacifist. RE-BASELINED in batch 15 T1 (the human playtest fix — goblin awe is now earned by TALKING while giving ground, and permanently blocked once the goblin has struck you; see src/game.rs's Game::resolve_awe doc comment). This is a real, expected drop from batch 13's 51.0%: a silent retreat no longer builds awe by itself (it only arms Monster.yielded), so becalming a goblin now needs a SUBSEQUENT talk while still armed, and that talk's own persuasion roll can fail — a failed roll lets the goblin's ordinary attack land, which permanently disqualifies it from ever being awed (Monster.struck_player). The bot (src/headless.rs's cornered-goblin branch) implements the two-beat rhythm: retreat to arm, then talk to consume; once struck, it stops wasting turns retreating (awe is hopeless for that goblin) and falls straight to the ordinary talk-regard mercy path instead (Monster::talk_threshold, unaffected by struck_player) every turn. Measured: wins 1811/5000 (36.2%), deaths_combat 3176, deaths_dark 13, stuck 0, kills_total 0 (pacifist_never_attacks still holds). THE FLIP STILL HOLDS: diplomacy remains ABOVE violence (diplomat 36.2% vs the violent bot's 32.3%, tests/tactical-band.json) — narrower than batch 13's 51.0%-vs-33.9% margin, but still the reliably-better-than-violence path the arc's mercy-economy design requires. Band brackets the measured value with regression headroom; the 50 ceiling keeps the design's own 'too generous' guard (batch 13's [45,60] top preserved as this batch's own ceiling, since diplomacy could still climb back there under a future re-tune). Calibrated for 5000 seeds.
